# Review of iliad-127 (20.1–102)

Two passes over units.json (the second also reading gloss.json, which was present). `t` untouched (checked: the
words of every `t` equal lines 1–102 of the pinned source). All notes stay within 25–110 words. Repeated whole
units (20.19, 20.82) match the published `l`/`i` exactly (checked by script). Line 9 and lines 3, 43, 44, 78 inside
larger units use the published wording.

## Hand scan of line 40 (flagged UNRESOLVED)

Λη-τὼ | τε Ξάν | θός τε φι | λο-μει | δὴς τἀ-φρο | δί-τη. Foot 3 is a dactyl, foot 4 needs a long first syllable but
φιλομειδής with one μ gives λο short (the scanner's “lengthening” flag); with the doubled-μ form φιλομμειδής (λομ-μει)
the line is regular. Foot 5 needs the syllable before φρ short (no position). The irregularity is real as printed; the
note says so in one sentence and now states the Ἀφροδίτη point correctly. Confirmed.

## Considered and refused

- λαοσσόος “rouser of the people” (units 25, 40): the Odyssey row's `l` is “people-rousing”, but the published Iliad
  parts (iliad-078, iliad-112) already ship “rouser of the people” in `l` for the same epithet; consistency inside the
  Iliad wins.
- σύμβαλον `l` “threw” / `i` “drove … together” (54): not contradictory; i is a freer but faithful rendering.
- κελεύω “commanded”/“ordered”/“told” in units 2, 1 (4–6): all inside the table's range (ordered/told; “commanded” not turned down for κελεύω).
- κύδανον “exulted” and βλεμεαίνων “exulting” (units 23, 21): same English for two Greek words, but each follows its own row (the new κύδανον row, and 9.237/8.337); no better distinct word is available without breaking a row.
- Πριαμίδεω `l` “the son of Priam” (77): the table (3.356) has this for the genitive; kept.
- φρένα τέρψομαι “accusative of respect” (22): defensible for the middle; l/i read it as object, same sense.
- ὅθ’ ὁρῶντο “middle form … they saw” (44): acceptable label (middle form, active sense).
- Unit 0 i “the Trojans were drawn up” supplying a verb absent from 3: it is the published wording for 20.3 (iliad-064), reused as required.
- Opening “ on Apollo's speech marks and mark strings (“Poseidon speaks”, “Zeus answers”, “Apollo speaks”, “Aeneas answers”): correct on the first unit of each of the four speeches; closings on 18, 29, 85 (and now 102).
- Paragraph flags p on 1, 13, 19, 31, 41, 54, 75, 86 match the packet's ¶; `ln` values all checked against the lines.
- Line-boundary claims in notes (“line 32”, “line 34”, “line 40”, “line 48”, “line 74”, “line 4”): all checked; only the 35 → 34 one was wrong.

## new-renderings.md against the table

Every row is consistent with the table. κύδανον, ἀκερσεκόμης, σῶκος, ὑπέρθυμος, ἀπειρεσίη, ἄναξ ἐνέρων, ἐναντίον,
νηκούστησε, τίθει φάος, ἶσον τείνειεν πολέμου τέλος, ἀγῶνα νεῶν are new and do not collide with a reserved word
(“against”, “boundless”, “high-hearted” are free). One note: the file's ἐναντίον row and unit 49 are consistent with
the unit's `l`/`i`. The ἀγών row's reasoning (not “assembly”) holds.

## Remembered English

Nothing found that arrives ready-made; the two places that read as stock English (“insatiate of battle” in `l`,
“who cannot have enough of battle” in `i`) are the table's own words for ἀκόρητος.

All 84 novel forms and the `__broaden__` block were checked against their lines. Parses are right. One edit:
